<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|234|THE GOSPEL|CHA. VI.}}</noinclude>perisheth, but that endureth vnto life euerlasting, vvhich the Sonne of man vvil giue you. For him the Father, God, hath signed. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=28}}† They said therfore vnto him, VVhat shal vve doe that vve may vvorke the vvorkes of God? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=29}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, and said to them, This is the vvorke of God, that you beleeue in him vvhom he hath sent. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=30}}† They said therfore to him, VVhat signe therfore doest thou, that vve may see, and may beleeue thee? vvhat vvorkest thou?

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=31}}† Our {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 16, 4. 14. Ps. 77, 24.''}}* fathers did eate Manna in the desert, as it is vvritten, ''Bread from heauen he gaue them to eate''. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=32}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore said to them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ why we keepe the hebrue word, ''Amen'', & translate it not, See the Annot. ''c. 8. vers. 34''.}}∷ Amen, amen I say to you, Moyses gaue you not the bread from heauen, but my Father giueth you {{sup|‖}} the true bread from heauen. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=33}}† For the bread of God it is that descendeth from heauen, and giueth life to the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=34}}† They said therfore vnto him, Lord, giue vs alvvaies this bread. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=35}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, I am the bread of life, he that commeth to me, shal not hunger: and he that beleeueth in me, shal neuer thirst. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=36}}† But I said to you that both you haue seen me and you beleeue not. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=37}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Gospel in the Anniuersarie of the dead.}}∷ Al that the Father giueth me, shal come to me: and him that commeth to me I vvil not cast forth. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=38}}† Because I descended from heauen, not to doe mine ovvne vvil, but the vvil of him that sent me. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=39}}† For this is the vvil of him that sent me, the Father: that al that he hath giuen me I leese not thereof, but raise it in the last day. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=40}}† And this is the vvil of my father that sent me: that euery one that seeth the Sonne, and beleeueth in him, haue life euerlasting, and I vvil raise him in the last day.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=41}}† The Ievves therfore murmured at him, because he had said, I am the bread vvhich descended from heauen: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=42}}† and they said, Is not this {{sc|Iesvs}} the sonne of Ioseph, vvhose father and mother vve knovv? Hovv then saith he, That I descended from heauen? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=43}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore ansvvered and said to them, Murmure not one to an other: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=44}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Imber vvenesday in vvhitsonvveeke,}}no man can come to me, vnles the Father that sent me, {{sup|‖}} dravv him: and I vvil raise him vp in the last day. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=45}}† It is vvritten in the Prophets, ''And al shal be docible of God''. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 54, 13.''}}* Euery one that hath heard of the Father, and hath learned, commeth to me. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=46}}† Not that any man hath seen the Father, but he vvhich is of God: this hath seen the Father. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=47}}† Amen, amen I say to you, he that beleeueth in me, hath life euerlasting. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=48}}† I am the bread of life. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=49}}† Your fathers did eate {{sup|‖}} Manna in the desert: and they died.<noinclude>{{rh|||This}}</noinclude>
